Hi Lauren / team,

Great to meet on Friday — thanks for the time. As discussed, LatticeBridge is targeting a reference adapter to Redwood Private (VPC) that will be used by a handful of our joint customers for embedded chat and reranking. Before we scope an onboarding project we want a short technical validation: surface any major gaps in the reference design, confirm KV cache/streaming compatibility, and run a focussed smoke validation in staging.

I attached our adapter spec and a light smoke test plan. Key asks from our side:
- Confirm supported auth flows (OIDC / signed headers) and recommended secrets handling for the adapter.
- Behavior when a model falls back to a lower-capacity variant (latency spikes / partial responses).
- Whether Redwood's prefix caching will play nicely with our tokenization heuristics.

Proposed window: 24–25 May for a hands-on smoke validation. Can your team own the runbook + canary steps? If so, who would be the technical owner(s)?

Thanks — looking forward to the collaboration.

Maya / Lauren — I pulled together a short technical playbook and a resilience matrix based on the spec you shared. High-level notes:

- Auth: OIDC bearer tokens are the path of least resistance for the Private deployment. We recommend short-lived tokens with a vault-backed rotation for the adapter client. Signed headers are supported but require extra network policy configuration in the VPC.

- KV caching concerns: Redwood's prefix/KV cache stores token-keyed states; because LatticeBridge applies a normalizer we must align on a canonicalization step before caching. Options:
  * Adapter-level canonicalize(input) -> use canonical input for cache key (recommended)
  * Disable prefix caching for rerank calls (simpler but higher token cost)

- Fallback semantics: we can route to a lower-tier model variant using the same request ID and emit a structured fallback header in responses: X-Redwood-Fallback: model=redwood-mini, reason=latency_spike. The adapter should treat streaming chunks with "truncated=true" as soft-fallback and stitch on client side.

- Failure modes to validate during canary:
  1) Cold-start degraded throughput (measure TTFB and 95p latency)
  2) KV cache miss storms during high concurrency
  3) Partial stream + reconnect (simulate 50ms packet loss)
  4) Auth rotation race (simulate token rotation while requests are inflight)

Runbook (summary / day mapping):
- Day -1: Credentials exchange, peering confirmation, smoke payload staging.
- Day 1: Baseline smoke (auth flows, single-threaded generation, embedding + rerank). Capture logs.
- Day 2 AM: Resilience exercises simulated at 50% concurrency; Day 2 PM: fallback routing test and streaming recovery.

Owners: Sergio (runbook owner), Karthik (adapter integration & canonicalization changes), Marcus (VPC & secrets exchange).

Please review the attached matrix for the exact test vectors and expected pass/fail thresholds. If you want we can run the first half of Day 2 as a dry run without failing any components.

—Sergio
